title: From matrix multiply to a production LLM inference server
audience: Can write Python. Knows no machine learning.

papers.2307.08691: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
papers.1911.02150: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
papers.2305.13245: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
papers.2309.06180: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.2211.17192: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

concepts.title: Vectors, matrices and matmul
concepts.blurb: Why a matrix multiply is the one operation that decides how fast anything runs.

concepts.title: Softmax and why it appears everywhere
concepts.blurb: Turning arbitrary scores into a probability distribution, and the numerical traps in doing so.

concepts.title: Embeddings: meaning as geometry
concepts.blurb: Representing discrete things as vectors so that distance means similarity.

concepts.title: Forward pass, loss, backprop
concepts.blurb: The whole training loop, derived once, so that nothing later has to be magic.

concepts.title: Why RNNs could not scale
concepts.blurb: The sequential bottleneck that motivated attention. You have to feel this pain to value the fix.

concepts.title: Attention: query, key, value
concepts.blurb: Weighted lookup, written as a differentiable operation.

papers.note: Section 3.2 defines scaled dot-product attention, including why the scaling factor exists.

concepts.title: Self-attention and the quadratic cost
concepts.blurb: Every token attending to every other token, and the quadratic bill that follows.

papers.note: Section 4 compares self-attention against recurrence and convolution on cost per layer.

concepts.title: Multi-head attention
concepts.blurb: Several attention patterns computed in parallel, and what individual heads actually learn.

papers.note: Section 3.2.2 on splitting into heads and the dimensionality bookkeeping.

concepts.title: Positional information
concepts.blurb: Attention is order-blind. How position gets injected, from sinusoids to RoPE.

papers.note: Section 3.5 on sinusoidal encodings, and why later models replaced them.

concepts.title: The transformer block
concepts.blurb: Attention, feed-forward, residual and norm, assembled into the block everything else is built from.

papers.note: Section 3 as a whole: the complete architecture.

concepts.title: Tokenization and BPE
concepts.blurb: How text becomes integers, and why token counts never match your intuition.

concepts.title: Autoregressive decoding
concepts.blurb: Generating one token at a time, and why that single fact makes serving hard.

concepts.title: Prefill and decode are different problems
concepts.blurb: One is compute-bound, the other memory-bound. Almost every serving decision follows from this split.

concepts.title: The KV cache
concepts.blurb: Trading memory for time, and the memory growth that then dominates every other concern.

concepts.title: Memory bandwidth, not FLOPs, is the limit
concepts.blurb: Arithmetic intensity and the roofline model, applied to a decoder that reads more than it computes.

papers.note: Section 2 states the IO-awareness argument precisely, with the GPU memory hierarchy numbers.

concepts.title: FlashAttention
concepts.blurb: Exact attention made fast by never writing the attention matrix to memory at all.

papers.note: Section 3: tiling and recomputation, and the online softmax that makes it exact.
What version 1 got wrong about work partitioning across warps.

concepts.title: Multi-query and grouped-query attention
concepts.blurb: Shrinking the KV cache by sharing key and value heads, and the quality that costs.

papers.note: Section 2.3 (Multi-Query Attention), contrasted against 2.2 Multi-head Attention.

concepts.title: PagedAttention and vLLM
concepts.blurb: Virtual memory paging, borrowed from operating systems, applied to the KV cache.

papers.note: The fragmentation measurements in Section 3 are the entire motivation for the design.

concepts.title: Continuous batching
concepts.blurb: Why static batches waste a GPU, and how iteration-level scheduling recovers the throughput.

papers.note: Section 4 describes the scheduler that makes paging worthwhile.

concepts.title: Speculative decoding
concepts.blurb: A small model guesses ahead, the large model verifies in parallel, and the output distribution is provably unchanged.

papers.note: Section 2.3 (Speculative Sampling) gives the acceptance criterion and the proof that the distribution is preserved.

concepts.title: Quantization for inference
concepts.blurb: Fewer bits per weight, and the outlier features that make naive approaches collapse.

papers.note: Section 3 (Int8 Matrix Multiplication at Scale): the mixed-precision decomposition forced by emergent outlier features.
Section 3.3 (The GPTQ Algorithm), built on 3.2 Optimal Brain Quantization.

concepts.title: Design an LLM serving system
concepts.blurb: Capstone: given a traffic pattern, latency targets and a GPU budget, produce a design and defend every choice.
